transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because after my shifts as a cashier, I keep ending up buying these huge takeout orders. Like burgers, fries, chicken, desserts—honestly enough food for a family—and then I sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I go home.
Do you feel like you're in control while eating these large amounts of food?
No, not really. Once I take that first bite, it’s like something in me just clicks off. I’ll be thinking, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but my hands keep grabbing the next thing anyway.
Do you feel guilty after eating these large amounts of food?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I don’t feel good after, but I haven’t really sat with whether it’s guilt exactly.
Have you lost any weight recently?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed my weight going down or anything like that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating these large amounts of food?
I don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t thought about it like that. I don’t have anything specific to say there.
Do you ever exercise excessively after eating these large amounts of food?
I’m not sure. I don’t really track it that way. I mean, I might feel uncomfortable afterward, but I don’t know that I’d call what I do excessive exercise.
Do you ever use laxatives after eating these large amounts of food?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been using anything like that after eating, at least not that I’ve noticed or thought of that way.
Do you often eat large amounts of food in a short period of time without trying to get rid of the calories afterwards?

Yeah. That’s pretty much what’s been happening. After my shifts, I’ll buy these huge takeout orders—like burgers, fries, chicken, desserts, enough for a whole family—and then I’ll sit and eat almost all of it by myself before I go home. I’m not really doing anything afterward to get rid of it.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food happen?

For the last several months, it’s been happening maybe three or four nights most weeks. And honestly, since the foreclosure calls started, I don’t think there’s been a week where it didn’t happen at least once.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake after one of these episodes of eating a large amount of food?
I don’t think so. I mean, I might feel bad after and not be hungry for a while, but I’m not purposely going all day without eating or anything like that to make up for it.
Do you usually eat these large amounts of food when you're feeling stressed or emotional?

I’m not really sure. I mean, sometimes I feel stressed, yeah, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether that’s what sets it off. It just kind of happens, and then afterward I realize how much I ate.
Do you think your eating large amounts of food is related to how you're feeling emotionally at the time?

I’m honestly not sure. I know I’ve been upset or stressed sometimes, but I haven’t really connected it in the moment. It feels like I just start eating, and I don’t think much about what I’m feeling until after.
Do you think your eating large amounts of food is usually a response to feeling upset, stressed, or anxious?

I’m not sure I’d say usually. Sometimes I’m stressed or upset, but I don’t always notice that before it happens. It’s more like I realize afterward that maybe I wasn’t feeling great, but in the moment I’m not really thinking about it.
Do you think your eating large amounts of food is ever a way for you to try to feel better when you're upset or stressed?

Maybe sometimes, but I’m not really sure. I don’t think, like, “I’m upset, I’ll eat to feel better.” It’s more that I start eating and only later wonder if I was stressed or trying to calm down or something.
Do you think eating large amounts of food helps you feel better when you're upset or stressed?
I don’t really know. Maybe for a little bit I’m distracted, but I can’t say I actually feel better. I usually don’t notice what I’m feeling clearly enough at the time to tell.
Do you think eating large amounts of food is a way for you to deal with your emotions?
I’m not really sure. It might be sometimes, but I don’t think of it that way when it’s happening. I just start eating, and later I wonder if there was something emotional behind it.
Do you think eating large amounts of food is something you do to try to make yourself feel better when you're emotionally upset?

I’m not sure I can say that. I don’t usually notice it as, like, “I’m upset, so I’m going to eat to feel better.” Sometimes I wonder afterward if that was part of it, but in the moment it’s not that clear to me.
Do you think you eat large amounts of food as a way to try to deal with your emotions?

I honestly don’t know. I’ve thought about it, but I don’t really catch myself thinking, “I’m emotional, so I’m going to eat.” It just kind of happens, and only afterward I might wonder if feelings had something to do with it.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these episodes?

Yeah. Once I start, it feels like something kind of switches off. I’ll be telling myself, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but I still keep reaching for the next thing. It’s like I can’t make myself stop in that moment.
Do you ever do anything to try to get rid of the calories after eating these large amounts of food?
I’m not really sure what you mean by get rid of the calories. I don’t think I do anything specific like that afterward.
